<action type="say">
I’m not able to place the booking through my integrated system right now because the provider search is rejecting all requests, but we can still get you help quickly.

Since this is an active leak, do these steps right away:

1) Limit water damage (right now)
- Look under the sink for a small shutoff valve on the pipe(s). If you see one, carefully turn it clockwise until it stops; that should cut water to the sink.
- If the leak continues or you’re unsure, shut off the main water to the house if you know where it is.
- Put a bucket/bowl under the leak and move anything that can be damaged by water. Put towels down to soak up what’s already there.

2) Get an emergency plumber to your address
On your phone/computer, search:
- “emergency plumber Fort Worth 76102”
Then:
- Pick 2–3 companies with rating around 4.0+ and plenty of reviews.
- Prefer listings that mention “24/7” or “emergency service”.

Call them (don’t wait for online forms) and say:

“Hi, my name is Steven Park. I’m at 1234 Main Street, Fort Worth, TX 76102.  
I have an emergency leak under my kitchen sink, coming from the drain or pipe under the cabinet, not the faucet or shutoff valves. I need someone as soon as possible today.  
What is your soonest available arrival time, and what is your emergency service/diagnostic fee and estimated cost range?”

Also ask each:
- “Do you charge an after-hours or emergency surcharge?”
- “Do you give a written estimate before work?”
- “Do you warranty your work? For how long?”
- “What payment methods do you accept?”

Choose the one that:
- Can come the soonest,
- Is transparent about fees,
- Has solid reviews.

If you’d like, tell me the names of 2–3 plumbers you find and any prices/ETAs they give you, and I’ll help you compare them and pick the best one.</action>
